title: Adaptive quant profile guardrails and smoke validation runbook (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Safely enable FP8 profiles (E4M3/E5M2) on Hopper fleet by shipping an automated calibration + smoke validation runbook and runtime guardrails. This ticket bundles the guardrail configuration, a reproducible smoke validation suite, canary rollout plan, and automated rollback triggers. Background: prior FP8 activations encountered intermittent model-quality regressions concentrated in corner cases (long-context decoding, low-probability tokens, per-layer clipouts). We need a conservative, observable enablement path that lets Dedicated and Hosted customers opt-in while we gather telemetry for gradual widening. This work must coordinate with calibration infra team, telemetry infra, and release managers to ensure the platform can safely flip profiles at scale.
acceptance_criteria: Automated calibration job (calib-run v2) runs against golden seed set and produces per-layer quant stats within expected ranges for at least 95% of models in our canary catalog

Smoke validation suite executes post-activation and reports: token-level LM loss delta, generation ngram overlap, and API latency. All metrics must be within configured thresholds before promoting from canary to broad rollouts
Runtime guardrails: per-request fallback to INT8 or full-precision when per-layer outlier detectors fire; observed fallback rate < 0.5% during canary
Canary rollout plan scripted: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated gating at each step and manual override hooks
Runbook documented with step-by-step calibration, canary observability dashboard links, rollback commands, and incident postmortem template
plan: 1) Define golden validation corpus (diverse prompts: long-form, code, math, low-frequency entities). Capture deterministic seeds for evaluation
2) Extend calibration pipeline: add per-layer outlier detectors, per-op quant-stats, and consolidated artifact output (calib-report.json)
3) Implement smoke validator: runs a suite of generation and embedding checks; outputs metrics and pass/fail decision
4) Wire telemetry: create dashboard with token-loss-delta, top-10 failing prompts, fallback-rate, latency-percentiles
5) Canary rollout orchestration: implement staged traffic percentages with automated gating based on thresholds in telemetry
6) Post-canary analysis window (48h) and promote/rollback automation; update runbook accordingly
telemetry: Token-level loss delta (FP8 vs INT8 baseline): threshold <= 0.03 average per request
Generation quality: BLEU/SBERT/ROUGE anchors per prompt group, configured per-model tolerances
Fallback rate: percent of requests that trigger fallback to INT8 or fp32; gate if > 0.5%
Latency p95 and p99: ensure no >10% regression compared to INT8 baseline
Per-layer clipout counters and activation histogram deltas: use for fast investigation and tuning
smoke_validation_tests: Deterministic generation checksum: compare early tokens for a fixed seed; fail if mismatch beyond tolerance
Long-context decode stress: 8k+ token generation stability test
Low-probability token recall: present rare-entity prompts and assert logits/rank stability
Quantization-induced token bias detection: measure top-token shift rate (>2% shift flags test)
Throughput/latency smoke to validate batching interactions at 50qps
risks: Undetected regressions in long-tail prompts leading to customer-visible quality drops
Calibration jobs producing unstable per-layer scales due to dataset skew
Telemetry gaps delaying detection of regressions during rollout
Too-aggressive canary steps could amplify rare failures across customer traffic
mitigations: Conservative default profile activation: require two successive passing canary windows before promoting
Per-model safe modes: allow pinning to INT8 for customer-critical models via Console
Expand golden corpus incrementally using real-world requested prompts (anonymized)
Alerting that includes top failing prompts and auto-create tickets for triage
rollout_strategy: Stage 0: Internal dev cluster smoke (0% customer traffic). Do not proceed until smoke validator green
Stage 1: 1% canary traffic for 24h. Monitor token-loss, fallback-rate, latency. Auto-block on threshold breaches
Stage 2: 5% for 48h if green. Collect per-model reports and flagged prompt list
Stage 3: 25% for 72h with extended telemetry retention
Stage 4: Gradual promotion to 100% with option to pause at each step
